leak.title: A thousand people see you. Seven come back.
leak.line1: The 993 who dropped off already cost you money. You just didn't keep them.
leak.line2: Double the ad spend and seven becomes fourteen. Give people a reason to stay and a reason to return, and the same thousand are worth three or four times as much.
leak.note: Illustrative figures, to show where the money goes. Your own numbers get worked out in the free check.

items.name: Get found
items.goal: Show up in search, show up on the feed
items.symptom: Someone within two kilometres searches for exactly what you sell, and you are on page four. Meanwhile the shop down the road posts three TikToks a week and half the neighbourhood already knows their name.
does: 8 to 12 short-form videos a month, cut for TikTok, Reels and Shorts
Hooks written first — the first two seconds decide everything
Instagram and Facebook posts on a fixed weekly rhythm
Google Business Profile: categories, hours, services and photos corrected
Profile description rewritten around how people actually search

items.name: Get remembered
items.goal: A month later they can still name you
items.symptom: They liked it. A month later they want to go back and all they have is "that place near the plaza" — no name, nothing to search, so they pick somewhere else.
does: The one line a customer can repeat to a friend
Naming your signature item, plus a visual hook — one dish, one service, one colour
A recurring series people start watching for, not one-off posts
In-store materials unified: table cards, window decals, packaging
One look across TikTok, Instagram and Facebook — not three different brands

items.name: Keep them
items.goal: Don't lose the people who already found you
items.symptom: Someone watched the video, tapped through to Google — 23 reviews, newest from two years ago, two complaints nobody answered. They backed out and tapped the place next door with 180. You never knew they came.
does: Every new review answered within 48 hours, negatives first
Review request flow: QR code, table card, follow-up text templates
DMs and comments answered from a script library, not improvised
Profile info, buttons, hours and booking links all corrected
The questions you always get, answered on the page so nobody asks twice

items.name: Bring them back
items.goal: Turn a one-time customer into someone you know
items.symptom: You don't know who came twice. What share of revenue comes from regulars? No answer. So when you run a promotion you blast a discount at everyone — including the people who were already coming.
does: Loyalty system: scan to join, points on spend, points redemption
Stored value and packages — lock in the next visit instead of discounting this one
Automatic triggers for birthdays, holidays and customers who have gone quiet
Member dashboard: who is a regular, who lapsed, what share of sales they are
One member campaign planned and written each month

faq.title: The six things you are about to ask.

items.q: Do you film the videos, or do I?
items.a: You film, we do everything else. We send a shot list on Monday — usually three to five clips, thirty seconds each, shot on your phone during a normal shift. We cut, caption, write the hook and hand back finished vertical video. Nobody needs to come to your location and no camera crew gets billed to you. If you would rather we shoot, that is a separate day rate and we will quote it.

Either. Where the platform has an official scheduling API — Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok once your account is approved — you authorise us through the platform's own consent screen and we schedule from there. You click once and can revoke it any time. We never ask for a password, because handing one over breaks the platforms' terms and the account that gets suspended is yours. On accounts without API access you get the finished file and a caption, and publishing takes you about two minutes.

items.q: Can you reach Chinese-speaking customers too?
items.a: Yes, and it is worth asking about. More than a third of Greater Toronto speaks a language other than English at home, and a large share of those buyers make decisions on RED and WeChat rather than Google — channels most of your competitors have no presence on whatsoever. We write those posts in Chinese, natively, not machine-translated. It is $400 a month on top of any plan.

items.q: Is the loyalty system bought or built?
items.a: Built by us. Square Loyalty and Smile.io exist and switch on fast; the trade-off is a monthly fee that scales with your member count, your customer data sitting on someone else's servers, and joining a queue whenever you want a feature added. Ours deploys on your domain, the database is yours and exportable at any time, and features follow your business. If we ever stop working together you keep the system and the data — that goes in the contract.

items.q: How many case studies do you have?
items.a: We are not going to win you over with case-study numbers. They are trivially easy to invent in this industry and impossible for you to verify. Four things you can verify instead: the quality of the hooks on this page, how specific the free check turns out to be, the output volume in month one, and a live demo of the loyalty back office. If month one disappoints you, the remaining months are refunded. That beats any case study.

items.q: Can you guarantee views, followers or first-page ranking?
items.a: No, and we won't claim it. Anyone who does deserves a follow-up question about how, because reach and ranking both sit with the platform. What we commit to is output volume and output quality, and both are written into the contract.

cta.title: Start by finding out which stage is leaking.
